_comment: Per-commit pin file for scripts\hermes-update.cmd. hermes-update.cmd does `git checkout --force -B main upstream/main`, which destroys every local-only commit, then re-applies the `keep` entries below onto the new base. action='keep' means re-apply; action='push' means already pushed upstream (skip); action='discard' means deliberately NOT carried forward. Order is newest-first: update_from_pins.py iterates reversed(), so application is oldest-first.
_reconciled: 2026-10-12 (fifth pass). Every keep entry now points at a commit that touches files NO OTHER entry touches, so application order no longer matters and the old 'apply AFTER X' ordering constraints are gone - previously 6185a207ad and 2c89194f45 both rewrote agent/lsp/install.py and minimax's two pins shared a file, so each cherry-pick was order-sensitive. 6185a207ad is split into three entries and 2c89194f45 into one. Two hunks were DROPPED as superseded by upstream: the _WINDOWS_WRAPPER_SUFFIXES pre-loop in _existing_binary (upstream's _native_binary_candidates does the same ordering, per its own docstring) and a previous_names field the pin added to tui_gateway ProfileRow that upstream ALREADY had - it was a duplicate field in a Pydantic model and has been removed. Earlier passes: 2026-10-12 fourth (three-way-merge ports, now superseded by these splits) and 2026-09-30 third (drift audit; --verify gained the abort before the destructive checkout).
_coverage_caveat: TWO separate ways a green --verify can still be wrong. (1) It is FILE-level: it answers 'does a pin rewrite this file', not 'does a pin reproduce this change', so a local commit on an already-pinned file passes and is then silently dropped. Every local-only commit needs its own entry. (2) After a conflicted cherry-pick the WORKING TREE contains the pin's cleanly-applied hunks, so reading it to decide whether upstream still needs the fix reads your own patch back at you. Read `git show upstream/main:<file>` or diff against it. Getting this wrong on 2026-10-12 produced two wrong conclusions in a row: 'the update-check pin is obsolete' and 'the lsp pin is obsolete'. Both were false.
_how_to_judge_obsolete: Never judge a pin by a symbol name, a keyword grep, or a docstring. Ask what the code RETURNS on this machine. Concretely: upstream's _existing_binary preferred lsp\bin\, which holds an extensionless #!/bin/sh shim, and os.access(X_OK) is always true on Windows, so it handed back a file CreateProcess cannot run. Only reading the resolved path showed the pin was load-bearing.
_upstream_sha_rule: Commits 6185a207ad / 20967fa770 / 2c89194f45 / f672142f23 exist in NousResearch/hermes-agent but are NOT ancestors of upstream main, so they must be re-applied. If any later lands on main, tip_already_applied() detects the patch and skips it automatically and the entry becomes a no-op. The entries below no longer reference those shas; they reference local replacements that carry the surviving behaviour.
_local_sha_rule: All keep entries reference LOCAL commits, so they are durable only while the fork carries them. They are pushed to fork/update/2026-10-12-upstream-2588; do NOT garbage-collect the fork. re-point them if the branch is ever rewritten.
_not_pinned: Commits touching only scripts/hermes-update.cmd, scripts/update_from_pins.py and scripts/hermes-update.local-pins.json are deliberately NOT pinned. hermes-update.cmd stages those in %TEMP%\hermes-update-runner and restores them into the repo right after the checkout, so they survive regardless. Pinning them would fail outright: after the restore they are untracked, and git refuses a cherry-pick that adds an already-untracked path.

commits.note: fix(desktop): resolve the live release dir through one helper. hermes_cli/main_desktop.py. Adds _desktop_release_dir() and routes _desktop_packaged_executable, _swap_staged_desktop_app, _desktop_ancestor_in and _stop_desktop_processes_locking_build through it. Without it the updater writes one tree while the app swaps another, and _stop_desktop_processes_locking_build returns early (dir absent) so the running app is never stopped and the stage-and-swap fails on the exe lock. The macOS .app-bundle paths stay in-tree. Replaces 45f465034a + 194acdecdb (same file, same fix). No upstream counterpart.

fix(version): read release-candidate tags, not just CalVer, for the base version. hermes_cli/version_info.py. Upstream moved from vYYYY.M.D CalVer tags to rc.<n>-vX.Y.Z, so _calver_release_version finds a stale tag and reports a 0.18.0 base with a 30000+ commit distance for a modern install. Replaces 88149ac8c7. No upstream counterpart.

fix(tests): delete git checkouts with utils.rmtree_readonly instead of bare shutil.rmtree. Three test files. Git marks loose objects read-only, so shutil.rmtree aborts with WinError 5 on Windows. Upstream ships the helper but these three tests still call the bare form. Replaces b08dfc3000. No upstream counterpart.

fix(update-check): compare against the upstream remote, not origin. hermes_cli/source_check.py + banner.py. Still needed: _Checkout has no `upstream` field and _branch_remote() returns 'origin' for a fork checkout, so behind would always be 0 on the origin=fork/fork=fork/upstream=NousResearch layout this updater produces. Only the cache-identity dict genuinely conflicts; resolve it as upstream's fields PLUS the pin's upstream/co.upstream (upstream added forwardOnly to the same dict). Replaces b747fdb565. No upstream counterpart.

feat(minimax): register MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview in the model catalogs and pin default_aux_model to it. hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py + plugins/model-providers/minimax/__init__.py. Upstream still lists only MiniMax-M3 as the aux model and has no M3.1-Flash entry, so both halves are ours. Replaces f672142f23 + a8af64d0d3, which could not be split because both rewrite the same file.

fix(tests): pass observed env-var names out of band in observe_terminal. tests/tools/_child_env_fixtures.py. The observed-name list is ~300 entries and grew into a ~17KB command line, over the Windows transport limit, surfacing as a misleading 'unexpected EOF' from bash. Upstream still inlines it. Replaces 6c8a40119f. No upstream counterpart.

fix(guards): match hermes_config by forward slashes as well as backslashes. tools/file_tools_write_guards.py. SECURITY: this is the guard that stops the agent rewriting Hermes' own security config through a path-variant spelling. Upstream's _check_sensitive_path normpaths but does not normalise the hermes_config comparison itself. Do not drop. Replaces 20967fa770.

fix(windows): protect PowerShell expressions from bash eval. tools/environments/local.py (+259): _quote_windows_powershell_command and helpers. Every terminal command is wrapped in `bash -c` plus an eval, so PowerShell is parsed twice and bash eats $env:TEMP/$_/backticks first. This recognises a simple standalone pwsh invocation and re-quotes it. SCOPE, know before you rely on it: multi-line scripts, pipelines and here-strings return None and stay UNPROTECTED (the function bails on newline). The real fix is to spawn pwsh with an argv array instead of a shell string, which would remove the class and make this entry droppable. Replaces b077396048. No upstream counterpart.

fix(guards): allow parentheses in a workdir path. tools/terminal_tool_guards.py + tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py. 'C:\Program Files (x86)\...' is a legitimate Windows path the metachar allowlist rejected. Safe because the cwd is either shlex-quoted into the in-shell cd (tools/environments/local.py _quote_bash_path) or handed to Popen(cwd=), which the OS resolves with no shell; widening the allowlist cannot become an injection on either path. Part of the old 6185a207ad.

fix(backup): exclude chrome-debug profiles from the archive. hermes_cli/backup.py. That directory is ~696 MB of live browser profile state and made every backup slow and large. Part of the old 6185a207ad.

fix(lsp): resolve a bare npm shim name to its Windows wrapper. agent/lsp/client.py. The spawn path only handled a command already ending in .cmd/.bat, so a bare pyright-langserver spawned the POSIX shim and failed with WinError 193. Part of the old 6185a207ad.

fix(lsp): resolve npm wrappers before the staging dir on Windows. agent/lsp/install.py + agent/lsp/cli.py. DO NOT DROP, and do not be fooled by upstream's docstring: it says it probes the staging dir first, and that order returns an extensionless #!/bin/sh shim that Windows cannot run (os.access(X_OK) is always true there). _native_binary_candidates already orders .cmd ahead of the bare name, so probing the npm bin dir first is what makes pyright resolve to a runnable binary - verified: it returns lsp\node_modules\.bin\pyright-langserver.cmd. The cli.py half routes `hermes lsp which` through _recipe_pkg_for so an aliased id (typescript -> typescript-language-server) maps to its recipe; upstream's _cmd_which looks INSTALL_RECIPES up by the raw alias and finds nothing. Narrowed from 2c89194f45, whose _WINDOWS_WRAPPER_SUFFIXES pre-loop was dropped as superseded.

chore: apply 11 local fix(es) from pins after update - squashed bundle of the 11 pre-squash pin fixes. Never landed: conflicts wholesale against current upstream. Its one genuinely load-bearing piece, PowerShell command quoting, was re-implemented by hand in local.py (e8c1de37a9 above) and is preserved by that entry. The rest were desktop/tips/kanban/YAML conveniences scoped out deliberately.

fix(windows): normalize path separators in _check_sensitive_path and guard POSIX mode test. Never landed - conflicts against upstream's restructured tools/. Scoped out deliberately; it is a safety guard, not the terminal path fix, so it does not affect the /c/... or PowerShell-quoting classes that e8c1de37a9 carries.

fix(desktop/windows): normalize spaced git path to 8.3 short path and guard stdout/stderr against EPIPE. Never landed - conflicts against upstream's restructured apps/desktop/electron. Scoped out deliberately; desktop-shell only, unrelated to the agent terminal fixes.

fix(scripts): add explicit utf-8 encoding in update_from_pins (Windows footgun gate). Never landed - conflicts against upstream's version of that script. Scoped out deliberately: hermes-update.cmd copies its scripts from %TEMP%\hermes-update-runner, so a mangled read there is recoverable, and the file is ASCII-safe in practice.
